title: Bind the communications PATCH handler to the acting organization
working_tree_status: dirty (726 entries at completion; +2 are this task, the rest are concurrent lanes)
goal: Stop PATCH from mutating another org
resume_condition: The task is selected as the owner's next collision-free work item.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: PATCH resolves the acting organization from the admin context, never from a request body or query parameter, and pushes an organization predicate into both the read and the write.
evidence: app/api/admin/communications/route.ts PATCH now resolves the organization before touching any table. The whole diff is confined to the PATCH handler (lines 252-370); GET and POST are byte-identical to their pre-change state. Proof: the pre-change file was sha256 23a83257a2cc6d37884354f9b90c9f642aa2cc5135e22af60cc707b34edb418c, which is byte-for-byte the value ADMIN-022 recorded for its landed state, so the file arrived carrying ADMIN-022's GET gate change and every byte of the diff below is this task's. Post-change sha256 is 11d039f5da3ab2d07cc0f6dbc47342f63a1474919066d3bc6c3bb78ce255683d.

THE ORGANIZATION COMES FROM THE ADMIN CONTEXT, and it had to be fetched: withAdminAuth passes only { user, supabase } (lib/auth/api-auth.ts:226-232), so there was no admin context in scope to read an org from. The handler now calls the real resolveActingAdminContext(request, auth) and returns its NextResponse verbatim when it cannot establish a verified acting organization. That is the same resolver withAdminCapability uses, and its denials are passed through rather than swallowed: 409 acting_context_required with no session profile, 403 acting_context_mismatch when the x-acting-org-id header contradicts the selected profile, 403 organization_access_denied when the user is not an active member of the acting org and is not its owner and has no tour collaboration.

The org then goes through resolveAuthorizedOrgLogisticsScope({ userId: user.id, requestedOrgId: admin.orgId, allowedTourIds: admin.allowedTourIds }) and the handler uses scope.orgId, i.e. the resolver's VERIFIED return value, not the requested value. That resolver throws AdminActingContextRequiredError (409) or AdminOrganizationAccessDeniedError (403); both are surfaced with the real status through the module's own authorizedOrgScopeErrorResponse instead of falling through to the catch's blanket 500. There is no fallback branch: if the org cannot be resolved the handler returns, and there is no code path that reaches the write without orgId.

The predicate is in BOTH the read and the write, on both actions: .eq('id', id).eq('org_id', orgId) precedes the select on each of mark_read and acknowledge, and the same pair precedes each .update(...). Four occurrences in total, asserted as four by the source test. The predicate is part of the query, not a filter applied after an unscoped read - the update is issued with .eq('org_id', orgId) in the same builder chain, so the mutation itself cannot reach a row the scoped read did not return.

The organization is structurally unreachable from the request. The body is destructured as const { id, action } = body and no org field is read from it; the handler never touches searchParams or URL query parameters. Three tests enforce this behaviourally (a body org_id, a query-string org_id, and a spoofed x-acting-org-id header each leave the other tenant's row untouched) and one enforces it structurally.
A cross-tenant message is reported as 404 Message not found, identical to a message that does not exist, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which ids exist.

NEGATIVE CONTROL C (the org predicate is load-bearing - the required evidence): all four .eq('org_id', orgId) lines were removed from the route and the suite re-run. 8 of 15 tests went red, and the two cross-tenant tests failed on the SECURITY claim rather than on a status code because the state assertion is ordered first: 'refuses to mark a message in another organization read' failed with "expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []" - Expected [] / Received [ "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" ] - i.e. ORG_A's admin id was written into ORG_B's read_by. 'refuses to acknowledge a message in another organization' failed the same way on acknowledged_by. The source test failed with "expected +0 to be 4". The body- and query-string-supplied-org tests and the collaborator test also went red. Restored byte-exactly to sha256 11d039f5da3ab2d07cc0f6dbc47342f63a1474919066d3bc6c3bb78ce255683d and the suite returned to 15/15.
NEGATIVE CONTROL E (the source-shape guard can fail): with the route left correct, the source test's four-occurrence assertion was shown to fail in controls C and B above, so it is not a tautology.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A cross-tenant test proves a second organization's admin cannot mutate a team_communications row it does not own, including the read_by and acknowledged_by array updates, and that an authorized org still succeeds so the denial is not vacuous.
evidence: __tests__/admin/admin-communications-org-scope.test.ts, 15 tests, all green. The fake Supabase client HONOURS eq and in predicates against a mutable message store, which is what makes a missing predicate demonstrable rather than assumed, and it throws if the handler ever uses or() on this path rather than modelling it loosely.

THE UNDERLYING MODULES ARE REAL, NOT DOUBLED. lib/auth/admin-context.ts is not mocked, so resolveActingAdminContext really runs: the user_sessions lookup, the organizer-account profile check in loadOrganizationProfile, the active-membership check in loadMembership, the tour-collaborator fallback in loadTourCollaboratorScope and the capabilities load all execute. lib/admin/resolve-authorized-org.ts is not mocked, so the membership re-check, resolveExplicitAuthorizedOrgId, the events_v2/tours narrowing and both denial errors really execute. Only the Supabase transport is replaced. The withAdminAuth double defers to the real userHasAdminSurfaceAccess from lib/auth/admin.ts - the same function production withAdminAuth -> checkAdminPermissions calls - so the admin-surface gate is exercised rather than stubbed true.

CROSS-TENANT DENIAL, both arrays named in AC-2. 'refuses to mark a message in another organization read': the acting user is an active admin of ORG_A and the message belongs to ORG_B. Asserts storedMessage(MSG_B).read_by is still [], the response is 404, that NO write query was even issued (writeQueries() is empty, so this is not a mutation hidden behind an error status), and that the single team_communications read carried both eq(id, MSG_B) and eq(org_id, ORG_A). 'refuses to acknowledge a message in another organization' does the same for acknowledged_by, and also asserts the acting organization's own message is untouched by a successful request.

POSITIVE HALF, IN THE SAME SUITE, AND IT REALLY EXERCISES THE WRITE. 'marks a message in the acting organization read, and the write really lands' asserts 200, success true, AND storedMessage(MSG_A).read_by deep-equals [ACTING_USER] - the mutation is observed in the store, not inferred from a status code - AND that the single recorded write query carried both eq(id, MSG_A) and eq(org_id, ORG_A). 'acknowledges a message in the acting organization' does the same for acknowledged_by. A fifth positive test covers idempotency for a user who already marked the message.

NEGATIVE CONTROL D (the positive half is not vacuous - the CP-098 guard): the mark_read branch was made to `return NextResponse.json({ success: true })` before performing the write, i.e. a handler that responds correctly and writes nothing. 2 tests went red, and the decisive one is 'marks a message in the acting organization read' failing with "expected [] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]" - Expected [ "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" ] / Received [] - while the response status was still 200 and body.success still true. The suite therefore cannot be satisfied by a status code; it can return a plausible-but-false zero and it does so under this control. The collaborator test failed for the same reason. Reverted byte-exactly.

NEGATIVE CONTROL B (the WRITE predicate is independently asserted): only the two .update() chains were de-predicated, leaving the reads scoped (4 occurrences -> 2). 3 tests went red: both positive tests with "expected [ [ 'update', ...(1) ], ...(1) ] to deep equally contain [ 'eq', 'org_id', ...(1) ]" and the source test. Reported honestly: under this control the two CROSS-TENANT denial tests stayed GREEN, because the scoped read already refuses the foreign row before any write is attempted. So the write predicate is defense in depth whose loss is not observable through the cross-tenant path, and it is covered by a structural assertion plus this control, not by a behavioural cross-tenant test. Claiming otherwise would overstate what the suite proves.

FAIL-CLOSED PATHS ARE TESTED, NOT ASSUMED. 'refuses the write when the acting organization cannot be resolved at all' (no session profile -> real 409 acting_context_required, and teamCommQueries() is empty so the table was never reached); 'refuses the write when the admin does not belong to the acting organization' (session points at ORG_A, active membership only in ORG_B -> real 403 organization_access_denied from loadMembership plus the collaborator fallback, table never reached); 'refuses the write at the admin-surface gate before any organization work' (the real userHasAdminSurfaceAccess denies -> 403 with the production "Admin access required" body, and the test asserts the gate really executed by requiring the exact probe table order profiles, org_members, organizations, tour_team_members).

NO REGRESSION FOR TOUR COLLABORATORS. 'lets a tour collaborator reach their own organization and no other' gives the user no active membership in the acting org, a confirmed+active tour collaboration in it, and asserts 200 plus read_by actually landing on their org's message, and then 404 with read_by untouched on a different org's message. This is why the handler passes allowedTourIds: the resolver supports collaborator narrowing for exactly this case, and omitting it would have denied legitimate collaborators.
STILL ENFORCES THE PRE-EXISTING CONTRACT: a missing id is 400 and an unknown action is 400 with no write issued.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The service-role client is either removed from this path or its use is bounded by an organization predicate the test exercises; if the existing resolveAuthorizedOrgLogisticsScope helper in lib/admin/resolve-authorized-org.ts is sufficient, that file is NOT edited - it is admin-governance owned.
evidence: REMOVED FROM THIS PATH. The handler no longer calls createServiceRoleClient(); it uses scope.service, the client returned by resolveAuthorizedOrgLogisticsScope, which re-verifies the organization before the handler gets it. A source test asserts the PATCH slice (the last export in the file, so the slice cannot be satisfied by GET or POST) contains no occurrence of createServiceRoleClient. The module-level import stays because the POST send path still legitimately uses it; removing the import would have broken POST.

WHAT BOUNDS THE SURVIVING SERVICE-ROLE CLIENT, stated precisely rather than glossed: a service-role client still exists on this path, because a service client is how lib/admin/resolve-authorized-org.ts verifies membership and the acting organization at all. It is inherent to the fix, not a leftover. What changed is that the handler no longer constructs or owns one, and every one of its four uses of team_communications carries .eq('org_id', orgId) in the query - two reads, two writes - so the RLS bypass is bounded by an organization predicate the test exercises. The predicate appears four times and the suite asserts four, and controls B and C each showed that assertion going red when the predicate is removed from the writes or from both.

PROVEN BY ORDER, NOT BY COMMENT. 'takes its service client from the authorized scope, after the resolver has run' asserts that in the recorded service-client query order, the first team_communications query comes after org_members, organizer_accounts, events_v2 and tours, and that the events_v2 query itself was issued with eq(org_id, ORG_A). A handler that built its own client and skipped the resolver would fail this.

NO MIGRATION. No schema, RLS policy, index or column is involved; the fix is entirely in the query the route issues. No migration was authored, none was applied, and nothing was run against any database.

Read the ADMIN-016 analyzer (__tests__/admin/support/admin-route-guard-proof.ts) and the registry entry for this route before editing, and used it to decide the wrapper question on machine evidence rather than taste. guardClassFor promotes a handler to capability_gated on withAdminCapability/withOrgCommand or on a call to hasAdminCapability/requireAdminCapability; read_only_compat is returned at the withAdminAuth branch, before the AUTH_PRIMITIVES branch that contains resolveActingAdminContext. So keeping withAdminAuth and calling resolveActingAdminContext inside the body provably leaves the method classified read_only_compat, and proveAdminRouteEntry would have errored with "legacy_pending_migration but the source already enforces capability_gated" had the wrapper changed. That is why the wrapper was left alone, and it is confirmed after the fact by the proof harness and check:admin-route-registry both staying byte-identical.

Implemented the fix in app/api/admin/communications/route.ts, confined to the PATCH handler. Diff: resolve the acting context and pass its NextResponse through on failure; resolve the authorized scope and surface its real 403/409 via authorizedOrgScopeErrorResponse; use scope.service and scope.orgId; add the org predicate to both reads and both writes; .single() -> .maybeSingle() so a legitimate zero-row cross-tenant result is not expressed as a PostgREST error. GET and POST untouched.

One deliberate product decision recorded: the handler passes allowedTourIds: admin.allowedTourIds. The resolver documents that parameter as already verified by the acting-context layer for tour collaborators, and without it a legitimate tour collaborator - who has no active membership in the acting organization - would be denied mark_read on their own organization's messages. That would be a false denial introduced by this fix. It does not widen scope: the collaborator branch still verifies a tour in that organization server-side, and a test proves the collaborator can reach their own org's message and not another org's.
